# Independent audit: identical-body pair versus twice ordinary depth


candidate cf676492f27e8f72,
including its Section 5 simplex identity. No mathematical correction
is required.

## 1. The actual pyramid and every ordinary normal

The displayed pyramid is a full-dimensional convex body of volume 4/3.
The point (0,0,19/25) is in its interior. The representation
(ZU,ZV_0,Z), with independent uniform U,V_0 on [-1,1] and density
3z^2 for Z, gives exactly its normalized volume law: the physical
Jacobian is z^2 and the normalization is 3/4.

A nonzero normal with zero z coefficient cuts exactly half the volume
by horizontal reflection; its boundary is null. Reversing a normal
with negative z coefficient yields the complement of a positive
coefficient cap, also with a null boundary. Thus checking both tails
for every positive z coefficient really exhausts all directions.

The conditional probability phi(w) in (6) correctly saturates at zero
whenever 1+w<=c. In particular it never applies a negative denominator
formula to w<=-1. The horizontal projection is exactly the convolution
of two centered uniform intervals. Formula (7) reproduces its density
and has mixing mass one; the limiting cases B=0 and A=B=0 are separately
covered. When A=B, no atom is introduced at the zero-radius endpoint.

I independently integrated phi over [-v,v]. This gives both formulas
in (8), including the uncut interval's contribution to the denominator
in the saturated regime. The first branch is decreasing. Its endpoint
gap is the displayed positive rational number. The second branch
clears to precisely

    3814 v^3+3253 v^2-4936 v+2484.

The quadratic discriminant is -7957712, with positive leading
coefficient, and the cubic term is nonnegative on the whole relevant
domain. Therefore every positive-coefficient cap has strictly more
than c^3 of the total volume.

For the complementary tail, pairing v and -v gives (12) by convexity
of x^-3 on its positive domain. Beyond v=1-c the negative argument's
tail equals one, so (13) applies without a spurious denominator.
Symmetry of the entire projection law is sufficient for this half
of the argument. Thus every negative-coefficient cap has mass at
least c^3 V. The horizontal cap z<=c attains c^3 V.
This proves the exact ordinary depth for all normals, not merely
for coordinate or symmetry directions.

Any halfspace containing the point can be tightened to pass through
it with no increase of mass. Consequently there is no omitted
containing-halfspace case.

## 2. The paired strict inequality and proper cuts

The paired thresholds 1 and 13/25 have total mass
(1-(13/25)^3)V=13428 V/15625. The cap at height 1 contains a square
face but has zero three-dimensional volume. This is consistent with
the stated closed-halfspace convention.

The exact gap from twice ordinary depth is 58 V/3125. Under the
proper perturbation, both thresholds stay strictly inside (0,1);
the derivative of the normalized cost is
3(1-epsilon)^2-3(13/25+epsilon)^2<=3. The uniform remaining gap
389/25000 for 0<epsilon<=1/1000 follows with the stated sign.
Therefore the strict counterexample is independent of supporting
boundary conventions.

The two copies at bases -1 and +1 give the actual indicated ambient
cap. Their convex hull also has the full middle fiber K; the source
note explicitly retains this fact and does not claim a mixed-body
depth counterexample after discarding that fiber.

## 3. The complete lower-diagonal simplex identity

For a>0 in the stated range, both rT_d and sT_d contain
J=((d+1)a)T_d. Its centroid is a*1. For any nonzero continuous normal
and any paired shift, restricting both caps to J and applying the
previously proved paired-centroid theorem gives

    pair cost >=2 Gamma_d |J|=2|T_d|(da)^d.

The zero-shift caps sum X_i<=da attain this value in both larger
simplices because da<min(r,s). The same argument works for d=1.
At a=0 those supporting caps have zero d-volume, proving the endpoint
separately. If one includes purely base-normal two-source caps, their
cost is at least the smaller full source volume, which is no smaller
than this bound since 2 Gamma_d<=1.

For equal outer radii, the ordinary lower-diagonal identity also
follows directly by ordinary Grunbaum applied to J and the same
attaining cap. No assertion at other simplex points is needed.

## 4. Verification

I reran supporting computation verify_identical_body_pair_below_ordinary_depth.py with
standard-library Python. It passes the exact polynomial/regime
certificate, 72 mixture-density checks, the strict rational gap,
100 proper-cut perturbations and the lower-diagonal algebra.
The all-normal and all-dimensional claims are proved by the
arguments above, not inferred from those finite checks.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
